questions.q: A neutral sphere of radius $r$ and density $ρ$ is placed in a uniform electric field $E$ that exists& on the earth's surface in the vertically upward direction.& If the atomic number and the mass number of the material of the sphere are $Z$ and $A$ respectively, then the& fraction of electrons that should be removed from the sphere for it to remain in equilibrium is [Assume that the sphere is able to hold the necessary charge without any leakage. Here ${N}_{A}$& -- Avogadro number]&
questions.solution:
Let us assume that we remove $n$ electrons from the sphere due to which the net charge on the sphere is $q = ne$

For the sphere to be in equilibrium

$mg = qE = neE$

$\dfrac{4}{3}\pir^{3}ρg = neE$

$⇒ n = \dfrac{4\pir^{3}ρg}{3eE}$
The number of moles of the metal in the sphere is

${n}_{mol} = \dfrac{m}{A} = \dfrac{4\pir^{3}ρ}{3A}$

So the number of metal atoms will be

${n}_{metalatoms} = \dfrac{4\pir^{3}ρ}{3A} \times {N}_{A}$

This means the total number of electrons in the sphere is

${n}_{total} = \dfrac{4\pir^{3}ρ{N}_{A}}{3A} \times Z$

Hence, the fraction is

$\dfrac{n}{ntotal} = \dfrac{4\pir^{3}ρg}{3eE} \times \dfrac{3A}{4\pir^{3}ρ{N}_{A}Z}$

$⇒ \dfrac{n}{ntotal} = \dfrac{gA}{eE{N}_{A}Z}$

$= \dfrac{ρR}{4{ε}_{0}} - \dfrac{ρR}{96{ε}_{0}}$

$= \dfrac{ρR}{4{ε}_{0}}\left(1 - \dfrac{1}{24}\right)$

$= \dfrac{23}{96}\dfrac{ρR}{{ε}_{0}} = \dfrac{23}{6 \times 16}\dfrac{ρR}{{ε}_{0}}$

$∴ K = 16$

(ii) the radius of the outer spherical shell of the spherical capacitor is increased

(iii) the radius of the outer cylinder of the cylindrical capacitor is increased

In each of these situations (i), (ii) and (iii), charge on the given capacitor remains the same but potential difference, in situations (i) and (iii), decreases, and in situation (ii), increases
In each of these situations (i), (ii) and (iii), charge on the given capacitor remains the same but potential difference, in situations (i), decreases, and in situations (ii) and (iii), increases

Each capacitor is charged and then removed from the battery. In situation (i), since $C = \dfrac{{ε}_{0}A}{d}$ , capacity will increase as $d$ is reduced. Therefore, $V = \dfrac{Q}{C}$ decreases, $Q$ being the same.

As $b$ is increased, capacity will reduce and

$V = \dfrac{Q}{C}$ increases, $Q$ being the same.

In situation (iii), $C = 2\pi{ε}_{0}\dfrac{L}{\ln\left(\dfrac{b}{a}\right)}$

$L$ is the length of cylinders; $a$ and $b$ are the radii of inner and outer cylinders, respectively.

As $b$ is increased, capacity will decrease and $V = \dfrac{Q}{C}$ increases, $Q$ being the same

The charge flowing through ${C}_{4}$ is

${q}_{4} = {C}_{4} \times V = 4{C}_{V}$

The series combination of ${C}_{1}, {C}_{2}and{C}_{3}$

$\dfrac{1}{{C}^{′}} = \dfrac{1}{C} + \dfrac{1}{2C} + \dfrac{1}{3C}$

$\dfrac{1}{{C}^{′}} = \dfrac{6 + 3 + 2}{6C} = \dfrac{11}{6C} ⇒ {C}^{′} = \dfrac{6C}{11}$

Now, ${C}^{′}and{C}_{4}$ form parallel combination giving

${C " = C′ + C}_{4} = \dfrac{6C}{11} + 4C = \dfrac{50C}{11}$

Net Charge, $q = C " V = \dfrac{50}{11}CV$

${q}^{′} = q - {q}_{4} = \dfrac{50}{11}CV - 4CV = \dfrac{6CV}{11}$

Total Charge flowing through ${C}_{1}, {C}_{2}$ and ${C}_{3}$ will be

${q}^{′} = q - {q}_{4} = \dfrac{50}{11}CV - 4CV = \dfrac{6CV}{11}$

Since, ${C}_{1}, {C}_{2}, {C}_{3}$ are in series combination. Hence, charge flowing through these will be same

Hence, ${q}_{2} = {q}_{1} = {q}_{3} = {q}^{′} = \dfrac{6CV}{11}$

Thus, $\dfrac{{q}_{2}}{{q}_{4}} = \dfrac{\dfrac{6CV}{11}}{4CV} = \dfrac{3}{22}$

questions.q: What is the radius (in cm) of the imaginary concentric sphere that divides the electrostatic field of a metal sphere of a radius $20cm$ & a charge of $8\text{\mu C}$ in two regions of identical energy?
questions.solution:
The energy between shell $1 \text{ and } 2 = energy$ behind shell 2.

energy between shall $\text{1 \text{ and } 2 =}\mathop{∫}_{r = a}^{r = b}\dfrac{1}{2}{\text{ε}}_{0}{\left[\dfrac{KQ}{{r}^{2}}\right]}^{2} \times 4\text{\pi}{r}^{2}dr$




$= \dfrac{{ε}_{0}{K}^{2}{Q}^{2}}{2} \times 4\text{\pi}{\left[- \dfrac{1}{r}\right]}_{a}^{b} = \dfrac{{ε}_{0}{K}^{2}{Q}^{2}}{2}\left[\dfrac{1}{a} - \dfrac{1}{b}\right]$

Energy beyond shell $2 = \mathop{∫}_{r = b}^{r = \infty}\dfrac{1}{2}{ε}_{0}{\left[\dfrac{KQ}{{r}^{2}}\right]}^{2} \times 4\text{\pi}{r}^{2}dr$

$= \dfrac{1}{2}{\in}_{0}{K}^{2}{Q}^{2} \times 4\text{\pi}\left[\dfrac{1}{b}\right]$

$∴ \dfrac{1}{2}{ε}_{0}{K}^{2}{Q}^{2} \times 4\text{\pi}\left[\dfrac{1}{a} - \dfrac{1}{b}\right]$

$= \dfrac{1}{2}{ε}_{0}{K}^{2}{Q}^{2} \times 4\text{\pi}\left[\dfrac{1}{b}\right]$

$\dfrac{1}{a} = \dfrac{2}{b}$

$\text{b} = \text{2a}$

$\text{a} = \text{20 cm}$

$\text{b} = \text{40 cm}$
